snippet.description:
Silicon Valley says it can build better weapons, faster and cheaper than traditional defense contractors. But what happens when the companies making those weapons also get a say in how they’re used?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In today’s episode, Vox reporter and producer Miles Bryan talks with long-time national security journalist Sharon Weinberger, author of Valley of Death: How Big Tech Is Fueling the Future of War. The book traces Silicon Valley’s deep ties to the military and its return to the weapons business through companies like Palantir, SpaceX, and Anduril. Sharon says this raises troubling questions of how private funding gives tech founders greater control over military technology, and whether their promises of innovation justify risks to accountability.

In this episode, Miles and Sharon explore the surprising CIA contract that helped keep Steve Jobs’s company afloat, how “tech companies” sell their visions to the Pentagon, if their innovations live up to the hype, and whether tech’s disruption of the defense industry could leave us with a more powerful version of the same old system.

Host: Miles Bryan, Vox Reporter and Producer
Guest: Sharon Weinberger, author of Valley of Death: How Big Tech Is Fueling the Future of War

Chapters
00:00 Intro
01:29 What changes when Silicon Valley controls the weapons?
10:08 How did the CIA help keep Steve Jobs in business?
19:20 How did 9/11 bring tech and the military back together?
23:36 What are defense tech’s founders really selling?
29:15 Do Anduril’s weapons live up to the hype?
38:05 Who sets the rules for using privately owned technology?
43:37 Is Silicon Valley becoming the new defense establishment?

Today on this special episode of The Ranveer Show, we welcome Nora Fatehi. She is a well-known actress, dancer, and model who has appeared in several Bollywood films and has also been a contestant on the reality show Bigg Boss. She is one of the most loved Bollywood celebrities in India. 

In this episode, we talked about how Nora Fatehi left her home country and made a name for herself, breaking all the barriers. We talked about her childhood life, her life in India, Indian vs. foreign media professionals, spirituality, and more. We also talked about the truth about Bollywood, bullies that she has dealt with, childhood memories, most difficult alone time thoughts, feminism, her perspective on Indian men, and much more. 

This was one of the most amazing, fun, and raw conversations I have ever had. I hope you will enjoy this episode as much as I did and let us know your thoughts in the comments section.

Today on the show, we have with us one of India's most incredible Bollywood actresses Kajol. The daughter of Tanuja and Shomu Mukherjee, Kajol made her acting debut with Bekhudi (1992) while still in school. She subsequently had commercial successes in Baazigar (1993), opposite Shah Rukh Khan, and Yeh Dillagi (1994). Starring roles with Khan in the top-grossing romances Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995) and Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998) established her as a leading star in the 1990s and earned her two Filmfare Awards for Best Actress. Hoping to bring back Kajol, someone who’s so open-minded, high-spirited & especially a great conversationalist.

In this fantastic episode, we spoke about some of the deepest aspects of both of our lives. From social media trends to Bollywood movies. She opened up about her married life, kids, her lifestyle, life goals & more.
